title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment
abstract: arXiv:2611.06812v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: With the growing need for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications to speech, challenges persist in summarizing and evaluating conversations that lack a clear end goal. We introduce SAUCE -- a reference-free, fact-based evaluation pipeline for cross-lingual conversational speech summarization. It measures the accuracy and the fact coverage of a summary through the entailment between conversation and text. We compare SAUCE against several popular summarization metrics and demonstrate the effectiveness of capturing information loss due to transcription and translation error and identifying broken summaries. Crucially, unlike black-box LLM evaluators or dense embedding metrics, SAUCE is inherently explainable: it maps summary scores to discrete, verifiable facts, allowing users to pinpoint exact hallucinations or omissions. translated_title: SAUCE：基于对话蕴含的摘要分析
translated_abstract: 随着对大型语言模型（LLM）评估需求的日益增长及其在语音领域的应用，对缺乏明确最终目标的对话进行摘要和评估仍然面临挑战。我们提出了SAUCE——一个免参考、基于事实的跨语言对话语音摘要评估流水线。它通过对话与文本之间的蕴含关系来衡量摘要的准确性和事实覆盖率。我们将SAUCE与几种流行的摘要评估指标进行比较，展示了它在捕捉由转录和翻译错误导致的信息丢失以及识别损坏摘要方面的有效性。至关重要的是，与黑盒LLM评估器或密集嵌入指标不同，SAUCE天然具有可解释性：它将摘要分数映射到离散的、可验证的事实上，使用户能够精确定位具体的幻觉或遗漏。我们展示了这种可解释性如何帮助开发者系统地分析LLM行为。
tldr: SAUCE是一个可解释的免参考评估流水线，通过对话与摘要之间的蕴含关系衡量跨语言语音摘要的事实准确性与覆盖率，并能将分数映射到可验证的离散事实，从而精确定位幻觉与遗漏。
en_tdlr: SAUCE is an explainable, reference-free evaluation pipeline that measures factual accuracy and coverage of cross-lingual speech summaries through conversation-summary entailment, mapping scores to discrete verifiable facts to pinpoint exact hallucinations and omissions.
